extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: A total of 29,133 male smokers aged 50-69 years from southwestern Finland were randomly assigned to receive alpha-tocopherol (50 mg), beta-carotene (20 mg), both agents, or a placebo daily for 5-8 years (median 6.1 years). headline.funnel_interpretation: Egger’s test is generally not recommended when fewer than 10 studies are available.
headline.results_interpretation: The pooled analysis of 5 studies yielded an overall effect size of 0.76 (95% CI: 0.64–0.9), suggesting that beta-carotene is associated with a lower risk of renal cell carcinoma. However, this association should be interpreted with caution, as there was substantial between-study heterogeneity (I² = 53.19%), reflecting considerable variability across studies.
